boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of California-Santa Barbara
boards.description: Ten currently listed food and convenience destinations in Isla Vista with evening or overnight availability documented by UCSB’s A.S. Pardall Center.

cards.title: 7-Eleven
cards.subtitle: 6545 Trigo Rd, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Use this 24-hour convenience stop when you need food or basics outside restaurant schedules; confirm stocked items in person.
cards.short_summary: A documented round-the-clock convenience option in Isla Vista.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB A.S. Pardall Center lists the 7-Eleven at 6545 Trigo Rd as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Listed as open 24 hours Monday–Sunday; visit during publicly open retail hours.

cards.title: Deja Vu
cards.subtitle: 966 Embarcadero del Mar B, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Choose this burger-and-food counter for a late meal; weekday and weekend closing times differ, so check the listed day first.
cards.short_summary: A food counter listed into the early morning on selected nights.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB A.S. Pardall Center lists Deja Vu at 966 Embarcadero del Mar B until 1:30 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 2:30 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 11 a.m.–1:30 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday; 11 a.m.–2:30 a.m. Thursday; 10 a.m.–2:30 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Domino's Pizza
cards.subtitle: 955 Embarcadero del Mar, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Plan a pickup or delivery order around the day-specific closing time; the listed Friday and Saturday window runs latest.
cards.short_summary: A pizza option with listed service to 3 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB A.S. Pardall Center lists Domino’s Pizza at 955 Embarcadero del Mar until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 11 a.m.–2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 11 a.m.–3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Freebirds
cards.subtitle: 879 Embarcadero del Norte, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Use the listed 11 p.m. closing time as a cutoff for an evening food run; check the venue before leaving for changes.
cards.short_summary: An Isla Vista burrito destination listed through 11 p.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB A.S. Pardall Center lists Freebirds at 879 Embarcadero del Norte as open 11 a.m.–11 p.m. Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Listed daily hours are 11 a.m.–11 p.m.

cards.title: International Market
cards.subtitle: 6551 Trigo Rd #3, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Stop by before the midnight listed close for groceries or prepared-food needs; allow time to select and check out.
cards.short_summary: A market listed open until midnight every day.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB A.S. Pardall Center lists International Market at 6551 Trigo Rd #3 as open 11 a.m.–12 a.m. Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Listed daily hours are 11 a.m.–12 a.m.

cards.title: IV Deli Mart
cards.subtitle: 6553 Pardall Rd, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Make this a Friday or Saturday convenience stop when you need a later option; other listed nights end at 11 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood deli listed until midnight on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB A.S. Pardall Center lists IV Deli Mart at 6553 Pardall Rd until 11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and midnight Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 8 a.m.–11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 8 a.m.–12 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: PokeCeviche
cards.subtitle: 901 Embarcadero del Mar #102, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Time a poke or ceviche order to the listed midnight weekday close or 1 a.m. weekend close; verify availability before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A seafood-focused option with late listed hours in Isla Vista.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB A.S. Pardall Center lists PokeCeviche at 901 Embarcadero del Mar #102 until midnight Sunday–Thursday and 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 11 a.m.–12 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 11 a.m.–1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Teddy Rice
cards.subtitle: 966 Embarcadero del Mar STE A, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Schedule a weekend food stop here before its listed 2 a.m. close; the Monday–Thursday schedule ends at 10 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A food destination listed late on Friday through Sunday.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB A.S. Pardall Center lists Teddy Rice at 966 Embarcadero del Mar STE A until 10 p.m. Monday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 11 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday–Thursday and 11 a.m.–2 a.m. Friday–Sunday.

cards.title: Wingstop
cards.subtitle: 888 Embarcadero del Norte, Goleta
cards.notes: Use the daily midnight closing time for a late dinner plan, and leave room for ordering and pickup before closing.
cards.short_summary: A wings restaurant listed until midnight every day.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB A.S. Pardall Center lists Wingstop at 888 Embarcadero del Norte as open 10:30 a.m.–12 a.m. Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Listed daily hours are 10:30 a.m.–12 a.m.

cards.title: Woodstock's Pizza
cards.subtitle: 928 Embarcadero del Norte, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Use the day-specific schedule for a late pizza order; Friday and Saturday are listed later than the rest of the week.
cards.short_summary: A pizza destination listed until 1 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB A.S. Pardall Center lists Woodstock’s Pizza at 928 Embarcadero del Norte until midnight Monday–Thursday, 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday, and 11 p.m. Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 11 a.m.–12 a.m. Monday–Thursday, 11 a.m.–1 a.m. Friday–Saturday, and 11 a.m.–11 p.m. Sunday.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented UCSB places for studying, making, recreation, and campus events.

cards.title: University Center (UCen)
cards.subtitle: UCSB Student Union
cards.notes: Use the UCen as a central meetup point, then check its services, study areas, events, and building announcements before heading elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: A student-centered hub with services, programs, and places to study.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB identifies the UCen as its student union and a student-oriented environment with services, events, and study options.
cards.access_notes: Check UCen building announcements and unit hours before visiting.

cards.title: Storke Plaza
cards.subtitle: Outdoor venue near the UCen
cards.notes: Pause by the sunken plaza and reflecting pond; consult the campus events calendar to see whether a concert, rally, or program is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus venue near the University Center.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB’s events site describes Storke Plaza as an outdoor sunken venue near the UCen used for concerts, promotional events, rallies, banquets, and dances.
cards.source_title: Storke Plaza | UC Santa Barbara Events & Tickets
cards.access_notes: Event access and setup can change; consult the campus events calendar.

cards.title: The Arbor
cards.subtitle: Campus thoroughfare
cards.notes: Walk the Arbor between commitments and look for campus outreach; UCSB uses this thoroughfare for student interviews about the Gaucho experience.
cards.short_summary: A busy pedestrian route used for campus engagement.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB calls the Arbor the campus’s bustling thoroughfare and reports regularly setting up there to ask students about their Gaucho experience.
cards.source_title: All the Answers | UC Santa Barbara
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor pedestrian thoroughfare; allow for changing outreach setups and foot traffic.

cards.title: Pacific View Room
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, 8th-floor Ocean Side
cards.notes: Bring quiet individual work to the eighth floor and follow posted quiet-floor expectations; check the library occupancy dashboard before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: An eighth-floor library study area with wraparound mountain and ocean views.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB Library identifies the 8th-floor Pacific View Room and states that floors 5–8 are designated quiet-study floors.
cards.access_notes: Quiet-floor rules prohibit conversations and group study; special events can alter conditions in the Pacific View Room.

cards.title: UCSB Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Library locations across multiple floors
cards.notes: For a project meeting, reserve an eligible room through the library system or use a listed drop-in room; keep the group within the stated capacity.
cards.short_summary: Reservable and drop-in rooms for small collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB Library states that its group study rooms support groups of 2–10 and include both reservable and drop-in locations.
cards.access_notes: Reservable rooms are available to UCSB students, faculty, and staff; booking is limited to four hours weekly.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, 1st-floor Mountain Side
cards.notes: Use the Learning Commons when coursework needs a library workstation, printing, scanning, or specialty software; bring your UCSB credentials where required.
cards.short_summary: A library computing and study area with specialty-software workstations.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB Library lists the Learning Commons on the first-floor Mountain Side with standard and specialty-software Windows computers, printing, and scanners.
cards.access_notes: UCSB students, staff, and faculty doing academic work have priority; specialty-software computers require UCSB eligibility.

cards.title: UCSB Library Makerspace
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, 1st-floor Ocean Side
cards.notes: Drop in during operating hours for available equipment, or reserve a specific tool; complete the required Canvas module and brief training first.
cards.short_summary: A library production space for equipment-based creative work.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB Library locates the Makerspace on the first-floor Ocean Side and requires equipment-specific modules and brief in-person training for relevant equipment.
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by quarter and breaks; some equipment requires a reservation, online module, and in-person training.

cards.title: UCSB Library Nap Pods
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, 1st-floor Ocean Side
cards.notes: If you need a short reset between classes, use a designated nap pod rather than treating library seating as a sleeping area; follow building conduct rules.
cards.short_summary: Four designated library pods intended for short rest periods.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB Library’s conduct policy states that four nap pods on the first-floor Ocean Side are designated for short rest periods.
cards.source_title: UCSB Library Building Use & Conduct Policy
cards.access_notes: The library prohibits prolonged sleeping and use of its areas as living quarters.

cards.title: UCSB Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 516 Ocean Road
cards.notes: Plan an active break around the gym, pool, or fitness facilities, and confirm current facility hours and membership eligibility before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A recreation complex with gyms, fitness areas, pools, and a pottery studio.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB Recreation states that the Recreation Center contains two gymnasia, weight rooms, racquetball and squash courts, swimming pools, a pottery studio, and locker rooms.
cards.access_notes: Quarterly use is granted to fee-paying UCSB students; other users may purchase memberships. Verify current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Multi-Activity Court (MAC)
cards.subtitle: Behind the UCSB Recreation Center complex
cards.notes: Check whether scheduled sports have cleared, then use the MAC for available recreation; it also contains Fitness Center 2 and the Adventure Climbing Center.
cards.short_summary: A recreation building for multiple indoor sports and fitness activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB Recreation identifies the MAC as home to Fitness Center 2, a roller hockey rink, the Adventure Climbing Center, and space for several sports.
cards.access_notes: A valid Recreation Center membership is required; availability changes when sport clubs or intramural activities are scheduled.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission activities on and beside UCSB, with access details checked on August 13, 2026.

cards.title: Browse the AD&A Museum
cards.subtitle: UCSB campus
cards.notes: Plan a midday visit during the museum’s Wednesday–Sunday public hours; no reservation is needed for ordinary visits.
cards.short_summary: A free campus museum visit with exhibitions in art, design, and architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: The AD&A Museum states that admission is free and advance reservations are not necessary; its public hours are Wednesday–Sunday, 12–5 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday–Sunday, 12–5 p.m.; the museum notes free admission and no advance reservation requirement. Campus parking may require a permit.

cards.title: Meet up at the exhibition reception
cards.subtitle: AD&A Museum • September 26, 2026
cards.notes: Arrive between 5 and 7 p.m. to see the summer/fall exhibitions together; the museum lists this public reception as free.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled, no-admission gallery reception for the museum’s fall exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The AD&A Museum lists its Summer/Fall 2026 Exhibitions Public Reception on September 26, 2026, from 5–7 p.m., with free admission.
cards.source_title: Summer/Fall 2026 Exhibitions Public Reception — AD&A Museum
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for September 26, 2026, 5–7 p.m. at the AD&A Museum; listed as free admission. Campus parking may require a permit.

cards.title: Walk the campus labyrinth
cards.subtitle: Bluff above the Pacific Ocean
cards.notes: Use UCSB’s self-guided tour for a quiet loop, then pause at the bluff setting; the site is ADA-compliant and open to the public.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided, accessible reflective walk above the Pacific.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB describes the campus labyrinth as open to students, staff, faculty, and the public, and as ADA-compliant and wheelchair accessible.
cards.access_notes: Open to students, staff, faculty, and the public; use the self-guided labyrinth tour. No admission or purchase is stated.

cards.title: Settle in at Sands Beach
cards.subtitle: Coal Oil Point Reserve, UCSB west campus
cards.notes: Bring a towel or simply walk the shoreline from the reserve’s public-access area; leave pets at home and observe posted protections.
cards.short_summary: A public-access beach beside UCSB’s Coal Oil Point Reserve.
cards.evidence_claim: Coal Oil Point Natural Reserve states that public use is permitted without reservation on Sands Beach.
cards.source_title: Visiting — Coal Oil Point Natural Reserve
cards.access_notes: Public use is permitted without reservation; day use only. Dogs are not permitted on the reserve, including Sands Beach. Parking may cost extra.

cards.title: Take the Pond Trail
cards.subtitle: Coal Oil Point Reserve, UCSB west campus
cards.notes: Walk the reserve’s publicly permitted trail at an unhurried pace, keeping to the route and respecting the pet-free reserve rules.
cards.short_summary: A no-reservation nature walk through Coal Oil Point Reserve.
cards.evidence_claim: Coal Oil Point Natural Reserve states that public use is permitted without reservation on the Pond Trail.
cards.source_title: Visiting — Coal Oil Point Natural Reserve
cards.access_notes: Public use is permitted without reservation; day use only. Dogs and drones are not permitted. Parking may cost extra.

cards.entity_name: Coal Oil Point Reserve Public Tour
cards.title: Join a Coal Oil Point public tour
cards.subtitle: Coal Oil Point Reserve • first Saturday monthly
cards.notes: Check the reserve’s tour information, then join the easy two-hour docent walk to learn about its natural and cultural history.
cards.short_summary: A recurring two-hour docent-led reserve walk offered without charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Coal Oil Point Reserve says it offers free public tours on the first Saturday of every month and describes them as two-hour walks through the reserve.
cards.source_title: Become a Tour Guide — Coal Oil Point Natural Reserve
cards.access_notes: The reserve advertises free public tours on the first Saturday of each month; confirm tour details before going. Day use only; pets are prohibited.

cards.title: Hear a carillon recital on the lawn
cards.subtitle: Storke Tower lawn
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or sit on the lawn for the scheduled summer recital; the university describes the series as free.
cards.short_summary: Free outdoor carillon performances beneath UCSB’s landmark tower.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB announced free 2026 summer carillon recitals by the University Carillonist and Carillon Studio students on the Storke Tower lawn.
cards.source_title: News Bites — The Current, UC Santa Barbara
cards.access_notes: UCSB described the summer recital series as free; check the Department of Music calendar for individual performance dates.

cards.title: Catch a student recital
cards.subtitle: UCSB Department of Music venues
cards.notes: Use the department calendar to choose a degree recital, then arrive ready to listen; the series includes more than 40 recitals each academic year.
cards.short_summary: Free public performances by UCSB undergraduate and graduate musicians.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB’s Department of Music states that its Student Recital Series presents over 40 degree recitals each academic year and that these events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Explore our Events — UCSB Department of Music
cards.access_notes: The department states that student recitals are free and open to the public; consult its calendar for dates and venue details. Campus parking may require a permit.

cards.title: Go to a World Music Series performance
cards.subtitle: UCSB Department of Music venues
cards.notes: Look for an upcoming World Music Series listing and attend with friends; the department identifies these performances as free and public.
cards.short_summary: A public concert series presented through UCSB’s music programs.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB’s Department of Music says its World Music Series features free performances and that these events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Explore our Events — UCSB Department of Music
cards.access_notes: The department describes World Music Series events as free and open to the public; verify the individual event’s date and venue before attending.

cards.title: Do a library research session
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, first floor
cards.notes: Meet in the library and use its publicly accessible resources or computers; students have priority, so choose a time that does not disrupt study use.
cards.short_summary: A free, public-facing research stop at UCSB’s central library.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB Library says it provides public computers for its collections, databases, internet, and productivity software to UCSB users and the general public.
cards.access_notes: Public computers support general-public access, with priority for UCSB students, faculty, and staff. Check library building hours; campus parking may require a permit.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct UCSB Library environments, from staffed commons and reservable rooms to quiet floors and access-controlled graduate spaces.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, first and second floors, Mountain Side
cards.notes: Set up in the Library’s two-floor commons when you need individual or group workspace, computers, and nearby study-room options.
cards.short_summary: A multi-purpose commons with individual and group study infrastructure.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Commons occupies the first and second floors of the Library’s Mountain Side and includes study spaces, computers, and group study rooms during Study Commons hours.
cards.access_notes: Study Commons access is for UCSB students, faculty, and staff with campus ID during designated hours; current hours vary by day and term.

cards.title: Group Study Room 1560A
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, first floor, Mountain Side
cards.notes: Bring at least one collaborator and use this listed drop-in room for a focused planning session, problem set, or shared screen work.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor drop-in room for small-group academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 1560A is a drop-in Group Study Room on the first floor, Mountain Side; library group study rooms serve groups of two to ten UCSB affiliates.
cards.access_notes: For UCSB students, faculty, and staff in groups of two or more; this room is listed as drop-in rather than reservable.

cards.title: Sara Miller McCune Arts Library
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, first floor, Mountain Side
cards.notes: Choose a booth, desk, couch, or shared table in the arts-library area when you want varied seating alongside art and music collections.
cards.short_summary: An arts-focused library space with several seating formats.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sara Miller McCune Arts Library provides study spaces including booths, desks, couches, and shared tables on the first floor, Mountain Side of the main UCSB Library.
cards.source_title: Sara Miller McCune Arts Library opens for study, research and learning resources | UCSB Library
cards.access_notes: Located within the main UCSB Library; consult current Library hours and any room-specific reservation requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Pacific View Room
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, eighth floor, Ocean Side
cards.notes: Use this designated quiet-area room for individual reading or writing, and keep conversations, group work, and calls elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: A quiet eighth-floor study room with mountain and ocean views.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pacific View Room is on the Library’s eighth floor and is identified as a quiet study area with wraparound views of the mountains and ocean.
cards.access_notes: The Library notes that special events are sometimes held in the Pacific View Room; check current Library conditions before relying on it.

cards.entity_name: UCSB Library Fifth Floor Quiet Study
cards.title: Fifth Floor Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, fifth floor, Ocean Side
cards.notes: Head to the fifth floor for solo reading, drafting, or problem-solving; use headphones quietly and take calls outside the quiet area.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet floor for individual, low-noise study.
cards.evidence_claim: The fifth floor in the Ocean Side section of UCSB Library is designated for quiet study; group study and cell-phone conversations are not allowed.
cards.access_notes: Quiet-floor rules prohibit group study and phone conversations; Library building access and hours vary.

cards.entity_name: UCSB Library Sixth Floor Quiet Study
cards.title: Sixth Floor Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, sixth floor, Ocean Side
cards.notes: Use this quiet floor for work that benefits from sustained concentration, keeping keyboarding minimal and audio low through headphones.
cards.short_summary: A sixth-floor individual-study setting governed by quiet rules.
cards.evidence_claim: The sixth floor in the Ocean Side section of UCSB Library is a designated quiet study floor where group study and phone conversations are not allowed.
cards.access_notes: Quiet-floor rules prohibit group study and phone conversations; Library building access and hours vary.

cards.entity_name: UCSB Library Seventh Floor Quiet Study
cards.title: Seventh Floor Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, seventh floor, Ocean Side
cards.notes: Bring independent work to this quiet floor and leave discussion-based tasks for a commons area or a designated group study room.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-study floor near the Library’s seventh-floor collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The UCSB Library’s seventh-floor Ocean Side map identifies the floor as a Quiet Floor, and the Library’s quiet-study policy prohibits group study and phone conversations there.
cards.source_title: UCSB Library 7th Floor Ocean Side Map | UCSB Library
cards.access_notes: Follow quiet-floor restrictions; current building access and hours are set by the Library.

cards.entity_name: UCSB Library Eighth Floor Quiet Study
cards.title: Eighth Floor Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, eighth floor, Ocean Side
cards.notes: Use the eighth-floor quiet zone for solo study and keep calls and collaboration out of the area to preserve its stated purpose.
cards.short_summary: A designated top-floor quiet-study environment apart from the Pacific View Room.
cards.evidence_claim: The eighth floor in the Ocean Side section of UCSB Library is designated for quiet study; the Library prohibits group study and cell-phone conversations in quiet areas.
cards.access_notes: The Pacific View Room may host special events; quiet-floor access and Library hours vary by day.

cards.title: Graduate Study Room 2504
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, second floor, Mountain Side
cards.notes: Graduate students can use this access-card room for quiet, individual work; plan group meetings in a separate group-study location.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet reading-room environment for graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Graduate Study Room 2504 is on the Library’s second-floor Mountain Side, is for quiet study only, and is available during all Late Night Study hours to eligible graduate students.
cards.access_notes: Exclusively for current UCSB graduate students using UCSB Access Cards; the room is available during all Late Night Study hours.

cards.title: Graduate Study Room 2582B
cards.subtitle: UCSB Library, second floor, Ocean Side
cards.notes: Graduate students can swipe into this quiet room for focused reading and writing, reserving conversation and group work for other spaces.
cards.short_summary: An Ocean Side graduate-only room for quiet individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Graduate Study Room 2582B is on the Library’s second-floor Ocean Side, is for quiet study only, and is available during all Late Night Study hours to eligible graduate students.
cards.access_notes: Exclusively for current UCSB graduate students using UCSB Access Cards; the room is available during all Late Night Study hours.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten campus-adjacent Isla Vista corridors, each anchored by a documented named destination.

cards.title: Pardall Road: A.S. Pardall Center
cards.subtitle: Pardall Road corridor, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Stop at 6550 Pardall Road to use the center’s listed study, meeting, printing, computer, legal, and tenant-education resources.
cards.short_summary: A student-services stop on the main campus connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Associated Students identifies the Pardall Center as a community center with study and meeting space, printing, computers, legal, and tenant-education resources.
cards.access_notes: Associated Students lists the Pardall Center at 6550 Pardall Road; confirm services before visiting.

cards.title: Pardall Road: Pardall Gardens
cards.subtitle: Pardall Road corridor, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Pause at the small park’s seating, stage, and native plant station while traveling between Isla Vista and the UCSB campus.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped pause on the direct campus route.
cards.evidence_claim: The Isla Vista Recreation and Park District reports that Pardall Gardens has a stage, seating, and a native plant station on Pardall Road connecting Isla Vista and UCSB.
cards.source_title: Peaceful Pardall Gardens opens in I.V.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park destination on Pardall Road.

cards.title: Embarcadero Del Mar: Anisq’Oyo’ Park
cards.subtitle: Embarcadero Del Mar corridor, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Walk the pond edge and look for the historic windmill, then use the picnic benches or check the amphitheater’s public-rental information.
cards.short_summary: Pond, windmill, and amphitheater along the loop.
cards.evidence_claim: The park district documents Anisq’Oyo’ Park’s historic windmill, freshwater pond, picnic benches, play equipment, and amphitheater.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park; amphitheater rental details are provided by the park district.

cards.title: Embarcadero Del Norte: People’s Park
cards.subtitle: Embarcadero Del Norte corridor, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Use the open lawn or picnic benches for a low-key outdoor break beside Embarcadero Hall; bring your own activity if using the field.
cards.short_summary: An open-lawn stop beside Embarcadero Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The park district describes People’s Park as an open lawn with picnic benches alongside Embarcadero Hall and notes its suitability for informal field games.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor lawn and picnic-table area.

cards.title: Embarcadero Loop: Perfect Park
cards.subtitle: Embarcadero Loop corridor, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Follow the improved paths through native coastal plants, then find the Peace Monument and the solar-powered phone-charging station.
cards.short_summary: A planted loop-side park with a practical charge point.
cards.evidence_claim: The park district says Perfect Park has improved paths, native coastal plants, seating, a Peace Monument, and a solar-powered phone-charging station.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park at the base of the Embarcadero Loop.

cards.title: El Embarcadero: Little Acorn Park
cards.subtitle: El Embarcadero corridor at Embarcadero Del Mar, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Look along the fence for commissioned Isla Vista artist murals, then use the grassy area, benches, or picnic tables for a short reset.
cards.short_summary: A mural-lined green space near the oceanward end of the corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The park district places Little Acorn Park at Embarcadero Del Mar and El Embarcadero and documents its grassy area, benches, picnic tables, and artist-created fence murals.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park at the Embarcadero Del Mar and El Embarcadero corner.

cards.title: Camino Del Sur: Estero Park
cards.subtitle: Camino Del Sur corridor, between Camino Del Sur and Camino Corto
cards.notes: Choose an active stop: the park district lists basketball courts, a playing field, disc golf, a pump track, and community gardens.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use recreation complex west of the commercial loop.
cards.evidence_claim: The park district says Estero Park runs between Camino Del Sur and Camino Corto and includes basketball courts, a playing field, disc golf, a pump track, and community gardens.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor recreation complex; use facilities considerately around other park users.

cards.title: Embarcadero Del Norte: Isla Vista Theater
cards.subtitle: Embarcadero Del Norte corridor, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Check the current campus or venue calendar before going; the theater has documented use for screenings, performances, conferences, and lectures.
cards.short_summary: A flexible event and lecture venue on the north Embarcadero.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB’s Isla Vista services guide identifies Isla Vista Theater at 960 Embarcadero Del Norte and documents screenings, conferences, variety shows, dance, a cappella, and lectures.
cards.access_notes: Event access and any ticketing depend on the current program.

cards.title: Embarcadero Del Norte: Embarcadero Hall
cards.subtitle: Embarcadero Del Norte corridor, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Use the address as a waypoint when navigating the loop, and consult university event listings for community events or lecture activity.
cards.short_summary: A UCSB-controlled hall embedded in the Isla Vista loop.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB’s Isla Vista services guide identifies Embarcadero Hall at 935 Embarcadero Del Norte as a site for community events, UCSB staff offices, and UCSB classes.
cards.access_notes: Building access varies by class, office, or scheduled event.

cards.title: Seville Road: Isla Vista Food Co-op
cards.subtitle: Seville Road corridor, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Visit 6575 Seville Road for the community-owned grocery store; its official site says the public may shop and anyone may join.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing community-owned grocery on Seville Road.
cards.evidence_claim: The Isla Vista Food Co-op identifies its store at 6575 Seville Road, states that it is open to everyone, and describes it as a community-owned grocery store.
cards.access_notes: Official contact page lists daily store hours of 9 a.m.–9 p.m.; purchases are optional to enter, but products require payment.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of California-Santa Barbara, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented to UCSB’s campus, coastline, shared spaces, and arts programming.

cards.title: Start beneath Storke Tower
cards.subtitle: Campus landmark and carillon
cards.notes: Use the tower as your first visual anchor: pause on the surrounding paths, spot nearby student-media offices, and listen for the 61-bell carillon.
cards.short_summary: Begin with UCSB’s tall campus landmark and its carillon.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB identifies Storke Tower as a 175-foot campus structure with a 61-bell carillon.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Get your bearings at the UCen
cards.subtitle: Student-centered campus hub
cards.notes: Walk through the UCen to locate a central gathering point, then check its current programs and services before making plans for the rest of the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A central stop for campus services and programs.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB describes the University Center as a student-centered environment with services, programs, and events.
cards.access_notes: Check the UCen’s current information before relying on a particular service or program.

cards.title: Take the lagoon-side loop
cards.subtitle: 31-acre coastal lagoon on campus
cards.notes: Choose a daylight walk along the lagoon shoreline and look for the salt-marsh setting; stay on established paths and give wildlife plenty of room.
cards.short_summary: A coastal-campus walk centered on wetlands and wildlife.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB states that Campus Lagoon is a 31-acre coastal lagoon whose shoreline includes salt-marsh species.
cards.access_notes: Use established paths and observe any environmental or restoration notices.

cards.title: See what’s on at the AD&A Museum
cards.subtitle: Museum beside the Pacific lagoon
cards.notes: Drop in for the current installation, then use the exhibition materials to pick one work or idea worth discussing with a new classmate.
cards.short_summary: A free art stop with rotating exhibitions and programs.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB says the Art, Design & Architecture Museum presents rotating installations, special exhibitions, and programs, with free admission for all visitors.
cards.source_title: Art, Design & Architecture Museum — UC Santa Barbara
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; confirm current exhibition availability before visiting.

cards.title: Set up a library reset point
cards.subtitle: Central-campus study and research space
cards.notes: Find the building entrance and a study spot that suits you, then save the current hours page; building hours vary with the academic calendar.
cards.short_summary: Make the library your reliable campus study landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB Library says it is at the center of campus, serves students and the community, and has hours that vary with the academic calendar.
cards.access_notes: Hours vary with the academic calendar; consult the library’s current hours before going.

cards.title: Orient yourself at the Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Fitness, aquatics, courts, and recreation programs
cards.notes: Tour the public-facing entrance and review the facilities list, then decide whether a workout, swim, or program fits your weekend and membership access.
cards.short_summary: Locate UCSB’s main recreation complex and its options.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB lists gymnasia, weight rooms, racquetball and squash courts, pools, a pottery studio, and locker rooms at the Recreation Center.
cards.access_notes: Recreation Center use is granted to fee-paying UCSB students; others may need a membership.

cards.title: Head toward Campus Point
cards.subtitle: Coastal mesa by the lagoon and channel
cards.notes: Make this a daylight coastal stop: take in the junction of campus lagoon and Santa Barbara Channel, and keep clear of sensitive shoreline areas.
cards.short_summary: A named coastal landmark at the edge of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB describes Campus Point and Lagoon Island as coastal mesas between the campus lagoon and the Santa Barbara Channel.
cards.access_notes: Visit in daylight and follow posted coastal and environmental guidance.

cards.title: Walk Devereux Beach
cards.subtitle: West Campus shoreline
cards.notes: Use the beach map to plan a shoreline walk or tidepool look, checking conditions first and respecting the coastal environment and any posted restrictions.
cards.short_summary: A West Campus beach identified for walking and tidepooling.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB’s Environmental Affairs Board identifies Devereux Beach on West Campus as a place for walking, snorkeling, tidepooling, and easy access.
cards.source_title: Beach Maps — Environmental Affairs Board, Associated Students UCSB
cards.access_notes: Check ocean conditions and posted beach guidance before entering the water or exploring tidepools.

cards.title: Find Isla Vista Theater for future events
cards.subtitle: 960 Embarcadero del Norte, Isla Vista
cards.notes: Walk by the theater to locate it for another evening, then check the event calendar rather than assuming a screening, show, or concert is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A nearby two-theater venue for classes and events.
cards.evidence_claim: UCSB says Isla Vista Theater has two theaters at 960 Embarcadero del Norte and hosts conferences, shows, movie screenings, and a cappella concerts.
cards.source_title: Isla Vista Theaters — UCSB Academic Affairs Information Technology
cards.access_notes: Event access and tickets vary; verify the specific event before attending.

cards.title: Check the Magic Lantern schedule
cards.subtitle: Film series at Isla Vista Theater
cards.notes: If a listing fits your weekend, confirm the title, time, and venue on the program page, then plan to arrive with enough time for entry.
cards.short_summary: A recurring UCSB-linked film program in Isla Vista.
cards.evidence_claim: IV Arts states that Magic Lantern Films screens films on Monday and Thursday nights during the school year and Friday nights during summer, with free admission for UCSB students.
cards.source_title: Magic Lantern Films — IV Arts, UC Santa Barbara
cards.access_notes: Screenings are recurring but schedules can change; confirm the current listing. UCSB students are listed as free; general admission is paid.
